10.1016_j.jfca.2026.109612: Saxitoxin (STX), a highly toxic and stable marine toxin, poses serious risks to seafood safety. Conventional detection methods are hindered by complex sample pretreatment, time-consuming procedures and high operational costs. Here, we developed a new molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP)-based electrochemical (EC) and surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) dual-modal platform for rapid and selective STX detection. Gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) were electrodeposited on indium tin oxide (ITO) glass to serve as SERS-active substrates, followed by MIP fabrication using STX as template to create specific recognition cavities. Under optimized conditions, the EC and SERS modes exhibited linear ranges of 0.1–50 nM and 1 nM–5 µM, with limits of detection of 0.035 nM and 0.33 nM, respectively. The sensor shows excellent selectivity over multiple marine toxins, good batch-to-batch reproducibility (RSD < 5.73%), and satisfactory stability, retaining over 90% of its initial response after 30 days of storage. Spiked recoveries in razor shell, oyster, and clam extracts ranged from 90.3% to 117.2% (RSD < 7.4%), and results correlated well with the reference ELISA method (R² = 0.9917). Integrating MIP specificity, EC enrichment, and AuNPs signal amplification, this dual-readout platform enables reliable, portable on-site screening of paralytic shellfish toxins for food safety and environmental monitoring.
